name: Water Pitcher
summary: A simple vessel used to carry fresh spring water from the local well in the Red Cloud Mesa. Greatmother Hawkwind directs young tauren to haul it back to Camp Narache to instill the values of humility, service, and respect for tribal elders.

sections.title: A Lesson in Humility
sections.body: Though modest in design, the water pitcher serves as an essential teaching tool for the youth of Camp Narache. Resting beside the water well on the plains southeast of the camp, it represents the daily labor required to sustain the community. By asking a novice to fill and carry the heavy vessel to Chief Hawkwind, Greatmother Hawkwind tests their character. The chore demonstrates that no duty is beneath a tribal protector, reminding young braves that tending to the everyday needs of their kin is just as vital as wielding a weapon on the hunt.

faq.q: What is the water pitcher used for?
faq.answer: It is used to transport fresh well water back to Camp Narache. Hauling it across the plains is a traditional chore that tests a young adventurer's willingness to perform everyday labor for the good of the tribe.

faq.q: Where do you find the water pitcher?
faq.answer: The pitcher rests right by the water well located southeast of Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa, near where Greatmother Hawkwind tends to her tasks.

faq.q: Who asks you to fetch the water pitcher?
faq.answer: Greatmother Hawkwind asks young travelers to collect it. Her aging legs make the trek difficult, so she offers the task to eager youths to test their vitality and humility.

faq.q: Who receives the water pitcher once it is filled?
faq.answer: It is brought directly to Chief Hawkwind at Camp Narache, who sees the deed as proof that the bearer possesses the heart and dedication needed to serve the tribe.

angles.text: For young tauren coming of age on the Red Cloud Mesa, carrying the pitcher is an early lesson that honoring elders and aiding the community are the true foundations of strength.
